reconcile.note: Matthew Henry credits Moses with ordering the ark while Bezalel built and finished it, so Deuteronomy and Exodus describe the same object from two vantage points.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen finds Deuteronomy's ark-chest notice inconsistent with the Priestly Code's tabernacle law, a D-vs-P divergence of which this ark-maker attribution is one instance.

quotes.text: But the ark is here spoken of in a connection which answers exactly to that of the Jehovist (Exod xxxii. xxxiii.), and is quite inconsistent with that, of the Priestly Code (Exodus xxv. seq.).
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on Deuteronomy's ark notice versus the Priestly Code's tabernacle legislation.

sides.snippet: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood.
sides.verseText: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. Its length was two and a half cubits, and its breadth a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.

sides.snippet: So I made an ark of acacia wood, and hewed two tables of stone like the first
sides.verseText: So I made an ark of acacia wood, and hewed two tables of stone like the first, and went up onto the mountain, having the two tables in my hand.
